issue.title: gui: the model picker blames the provider for a group's listed=no, and names every group but the one hiding the model
issue.body:
### Version

0.1.1278 — macOS app (CLI and app are the same binary; both `sha256 d8c4436b…c6ca26`).

### Setup

- Provider `codex`: 3 exposed models of 7 (`gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-luna`).
- Routing group `night-shift`: **`listed=no`** (`Group.Unlists`) with members `codex/gpt-6-luna:max`, `codex/gpt-6.1-sol:medium`.
- The **Codex agent is set to `group/night-shift`**.
- Two other groups (`codex-budget`, `pure-codex`) contain the same two models and are listed normally.
- No provider has `Provider.Unlisted` set (`providers.json` has no `unlisted` key for `codex`).

### Steps

Open the Codex agent's model picker and type `sol`.

### Expected

The note names `night-shift` — the group that actually keeps the model out of agents' lists — and points at that group's "The group alone" / `listed=no` toggle.

### Actual

> Codex is used only through routing groups: agents reach GPT-6.1-Sol by picking Codex Budget, pure-codex.

Two problems:

1. **It blames the provider, not the group.** The "Only through routing groups" checkbox in Codex's provider editor is already off; the model is unlisted by the *group* (`Group.Unlists`), so following the sentence's advice ("untick … in {provider}'s models") is a no-op.
2. **It omits the group that did it.** The group the agent is currently set to (`night-shift`, the culprit) never appears in the sentence; the groups it does name (`codex-budget`, `pure-codex`) are innocent.

Practical cost: I turned `listed=no` off on two innocent groups before finding the real one, and the note is what sent me there.

### Cause (main)

- `internal/gui/api.go:unlistedModels()` merges `Provider.Unlisted` and group-unlisted models (`provider.Unlisted()`, see `unlistedByGroups` in `internal/provider/models.go`) into one `state.unlisted`, with no discriminator saying which mechanism unlisted it. So `keptNote()` in `internal/gui/assets/app.js` always uses the provider wording, and `internal/gui/api.go` cannot give the front end anything better.
- The missing group is a second, independent issue: `openPicker()` promotes the current value's row to the top as `{...c, group: "", home: c.group}`, while `keptNote()` matches groups with

  ```js
  const via = m.groups.map((g) => pick.options.find((o) => o.ref === g && o.group === ROUTING_GROUPS)).filter(Boolean);
  ```

  When the agent is *set to the unlisting group*, that group's option has `group: ""` and `home: "Routing groups"`, so it never matches and is dropped from `m.groups` → sentence. The picker then lists the remaining groups, none of which is the cause.
- The "in none, so no agent can use it" variant has the same problem: its call to action tells the user to untick the provider's checkbox, which does nothing when a group is what unlisted the model.

### Suggested fix

1. Carry the source in `unlistedJSON` (e.g. `byProvider bool` / `byGroup "group/<id>"`), filled from `Provider.Unlisted` vs `unlistedByGroups`.
2. In `keptNote()`: match groups with `o.group === ROUTING_GROUPS || o.home === ROUTING_GROUPS`, and word it per source — for a group: "…is kept out of agents' lists by {group}" with an action that sets that group back to listing its models (`listed=yes`), keeping the "Pick {group}" button; keep the current provider sentence only when `byProvider`.
3. A group case could be covered by extending `internal/provider/group_unlists_test.go` (`TestGroupUnlistsItsModels`) to assert the JSON carries the group.

The same English string is reused by every locale through the shared string table, so this is one wording change, not per-locale work.

Related (feature, not this bug): #2105 asks for one global switch for "listed=no" across groups.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/2746-unlisted-by-group` (head `e678dbc5`, on upstream `6eb510f7`) — the model picker names the group that unlists it, not the provider.

**Root cause.** `internal/gui/api.go`'s `unlistedJSON` carried only the provider, so a model a routing group keeps out of the lists was blamed on its provider — and the picker named every group but the one hiding the model (a promoted group row arrives with `group: ""`, so `via` was empty).

**Change.** `unlistedJSON` gains `ByGroup`, set when the culprit is the selected group; the picker's note matches groups by `o.group === ROUTING_GROUPS || o.home === ROUTING_GROUPS` and, when `m.byGroup`, names that group and drops the provider sentence and "The group alone". The two provider sentences are byte-identical (a test asserts them); the new wording is in all five languages with identical placeholders, and the i18n-keys check passes.

**Verified.** Red: `the new case in `unlisted-models.test.cjs` (a `byGroup` model, two `unlists` groups, the agent's field on the group)` → the note blamed `Codex` (the provider) and named no group
Green: `same command → 4/4 (chromium + webkit × en/zh); `TestCoreScriptBudget` unchanged` → `ℹ pass 4, fail 0`

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 27's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6eb510f7` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2746-unlisted-by-group — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.
